description: The pie chart visually represents the distribution of content categories evaluated in the context of attribution by large language models, as referenced in the paper “Automatic Evaluation of Attribution by Large Language Models.” The chart is divided into eleven distinct segments, each labeled with a category name and its corresponding percentage. The largest segment, colored blue, represents “Business” at 24.3%, followed by “Econ. & Fin.” in teal at 18.4%. Other notable segments include “History” and “Game&Anime,” both at 8.2%; “Daily Life” at 7.1%; “Med & Health” and “Science,” both at 6.7%; “Pet & Animal” at 5.5%; “Law” at 5.1%; “Geography” at 2.7%; and “Math,” the smallest segment, at 1.2%. Each slice is connected via a thin gray line to its label, which is positioned outside the pie for clarity. The segments are arranged in a clockwise direction, starting from the top-right with “Business,” and vary in color to distinguish categories. The chart does not include a legend but uses direct labeling for each slice, and no segment is visually exploded or emphasized beyond its proportional size. The overall visual suggests a diverse but uneven distribution of content categories, with a clear dominance of “Business” and “Econ. & Fin.” in the dataset or evaluation scope.
